name: 231. Responses instructions lead the system prompt ahead of developer input (instructions with developer)
description: Top-level Responses `instructions` were dropped whenever the input also carried a system or developer message: the Anthropic converter (shared by Anthropic, Vertex, Azure, Bedrock InvokeModel, Bedrock Mantle, Fireworks, DeepSeek, vLLM and SGL), Bedrock Converse, Gemini (and Vertex Gemini), Cohere and Replicate used instructions only as a fallback when the input had no system content. Codex sends its base prompt in `instructions` and app rules as `developer` messages, so the base prompt never reached the model and the request still returned 200. OpenAI places `instructions` ahead of the input, and the Responses-to-Chat fallback in core/schemas/mux.go already did, so now instructions lead the system prompt everywhere: a separate leading block for Anthropic, Bedrock and Gemini, joined first with a newline for Cohere's single system turn. Each case reads the upstream body from extra_fields.raw_request and asserts BASE_RULES (instructions) and APP_RULES (developer) both reach the system prompt, instructions first. 231.1-231.3 pin the Anthropic converter on /v1/responses, its stream and the /openai/v1/responses drop-in Codex uses. 231.4 pins Bedrock Converse, 231.5-231.6 Gemini on both hosts, 231.7 Cohere. Not covered here: /anthropic, /genai and /bedrock have no `instructions` field, so they cannot carry the pair; Vertex/Azure/Mantle Claude and the other Anthropic-wire hosts reuse the converter 231.1-231.3 pin; Replicate is pinned by its Go unit test only, since the harness has no Replicate text rows (its one row is image generation).
